questions.stem: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. What happens to the cell?

options.text: Water moves into the cell by osmosis, causing it to burst
The cell absorbs sugar molecules through its membrane
Water moves out of the cell by osmosis, and the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall
Nothing happens because the cell wall prevents all movement of water

questions.explanation: In a concentrated sugar solution, the water concentration is higher inside the cell than outside. Water leaves the cell by osmosis, causing the vacuole to shrink and the cell membrane to pull away from the cell wall. This process is called plasmolysis.
